info.title: MIDAX402
info.description: MIDAX402 — Independent verification for x402 services: we probe an endpoint, judge it against the x402 spec and sign the verdict so its signature is verifiable without asking us. Also pay-per-query intelligence over a curated x402 corpus, payable on Base Mainnet, Algorand Mainnet and Solana Mainnet. Non-personalized analysis of x402 ecosystem data, not financial advice.
info.x-guidance: How to use MIDAX402 (x402, pay per call, no account and no API key): an unpaid request to a paid route returns HTTP 402 with the payment requirements in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header; pay with an x402 client and retry the same request with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (some SDKs send X-PAYMENT). Payable on Base Mainnet, Algorand Mainnet and Solana Mainnet. Paid resources, in families that never mix: (1) intelligence tiers over the curated x402 corpus; GET ?query=... or POST JSON {"query": "..."}: /midas-ops/basic $0.03, /midas-ops/standard $0.05, /midas-ops/premium $0.07, /midas-ops/market_brief $0.15; (2) verifier ladder, judging any third-party x402 endpoint you name; GET ?url=... or POST JSON {"url": "..."}: /midas-ops/pulse $0.001 (is it live and charging), /midas-ops/verify $0.10 (full conformance check, private), /midas-ops/attest $0.50 (same check, signed and published); (3) authenticity report: the already-measured signed verdict for a target, never a fresh measurement; GET ?url=... or POST JSON {"url": "..."}: /midas-ops/authenticity-report $5; (4) challenge-readiness check: the five official Global Challenge requirements measured on one participant endpoint, signed, describing one instant; GET ?url=... or POST JSON {"url": "..."}: /midas-ops/challenge-check $1; (5) board position on the public verification board: it buys position only, never a verdict; GET ?target_url=... or POST JSON {"target_url": "..."}: /midas-ops/rank/1 $1, /midas-ops/rank/2 $2, /midas-ops/rank/5 $5, /midas-ops/rank/10 $10, /midas-ops/rank/25 $25, /midas-ops/rank/50 $50, /midas-ops/rank/100 $100. Free: /midas-ops/verify-before-pay?url=..., /.well-known/x402, /llms.txt. Allow a client timeout of at least 180 s for the intelligence tiers; a retry with the same payment is served idempotently.

get.description: MIDAX402 Pulse: is this x402 endpoint live and charging RIGHT NOW? You get a verdict (x402_live / x402_challenge_malformed / inconclusive / unreachable), the HTTP status, and checked_at + age_seconds, for ANY endpoint you name. PAYING BUYS THE CURRENT ANSWER, NOT A FRESH PROBE: cached per target up to 60s, so a busy endpoint is never hammered. One unpaid GET: it does NOT analyse the challenge, check price coherence or give a reasoned verdict (that is /midas-ops/verify).

get.description: Challenge-readiness check for the x402 Global Challenge. Send the URL of a participant's paid endpoint and get an EIP-712 signed verdict on five official requirements: GoPlausible fee payer in its accepts, Bazaar extension declared, x402-global-challenge tag, a real Algorand mainnet settlement to its payTo, a row on the challenge leaderboard. Each has its source, evidence and time. It describes one instant and does not say you qualify. Not charged if it cannot measure.

get.description: Read-only rolling metrics from requests.jsonl for the last 30 days. Keyed: the route requires ?key= and answers 404 without it. The example below shows the response shape with zero values, not live data.

200.description: Metrics snapshot (response shape; the route is keyed).

funnel_counters.privacy_note: Aggregated counts only: no IP addresses (hashed or otherwise), no user agents, no target URLs. The `mcp` channel is self-declared by the MCP proxy via a request header -- useful for attribution, not a security boundary. The `internal` channel is MIDAX's own measurements against production (User-Agent MIDAX-internal), counted apart so they never read as demand; it is self-declared too.

example.internal_requests_note: Requests that identified themselves as MIDAX's own measurements (User-Agent MIDAX-internal), counted apart from total_requests and from each tier's count. Only ledger rows that carry a channel field can be separated; rows written before the channel existed carry none and are counted in total_requests.
example.revenue_scope_note: `total_revenue_usdc` counts settlements on MAINNET rails only. Testnet/devnet settlements are real transactions but not money, so they are reported separately under `testnet_usdc` instead of being added or silently dropped. Rows whose rail cannot be classified are reported under `unclassified_usdc` -- unknown is not zero.

friction.note: settle/verify over payment attempts that arrived with a credential. Always read with n: a ratio over a handful of attempts is an anecdote, not a rate. Lower friction lowers the failed-verify count, so a transaction-count column that includes failures moves DOWN as this improves. MIDAX's own attempts (User-Agent MIDAX-internal) are left out of n and counted in excluded_internal.

get.description: Read-only, network-free view of the organization-grouped contact map (mision #217). The network extraction that populates it runs separately (contact_map_extraction.py); this endpoint only serves what it already wrote.

200.description: The grouped contact map, or a generated:false placeholder if the extraction has not run yet.

example.limits: Grouping evidence is registrable domain, an identical declared contact channel, or an identical declared repository -- never name similarity. A hostname that shares none of these with any other stays its own organization, marked grouping_status=undetermined rather than guessed.

get.description: Read-only, signing-free view of the registry's permanence anchor (mision #218): the append-only chain of daily Algorand seals that proves the attestation list was not pruned or reordered. Sealing runs separately (run_daily_seal.py, via algorand_anchor_scheduler.py); this endpoint only serves what that process already wrote.

200.description: The seal chain, or a sealed:false placeholder if no seal has landed yet.

example.what_this_proves: The anchor proves the attestation registry's LIST was not pruned or reordered as of the last seal's date -- it does NOT prove any individual verdict is correct (the EIP-712 signature on each attestation already does that), and it does NOT make the registry permanent -- what sustains Algorand's history is its archival nodes, same as pins sustain IPFS. See docs/ALGORAND_ANCHOR_SPEC.md for the canonical digest, the chain, and a publishable test vector a third party can recompute independently.

test_vector.description: Un registro de ejemplo y su digest esperado, publicados junto a la spec para que 'reproducible' sea algo que cualquiera puede chequear, no una afirmacion que nadie verifica.

get.description: Free, no-auth SVG badge showing MIDAX's signed verdict for an already-verified endpoint, with its age always visible. Returns image/svg+xml by default; pass `Accept: application/json` for the structured form. Returns 404 (`code: badge_unavailable`) if no signed attestation exists yet for the target -- no badge is issued for an endpoint MIDAX never verified. Purchased board position (see /rank) never appears on the badge; conformance_score never travels as a bare number, only as a verdict in words.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The already-verified target_url to render a badge for.

200.description: The SVG badge (default) or, with Accept: application/json, its JSON form.

404.description: No signed attestation exists yet for that target_url.

get.summary: Verify before you pay (free, reads the signed registry only)
get.description: The question a buying agent asks BEFORE paying any x402 service: does MIDAX have a signed conformance verdict for this URL? Fail-closed -- if no attestation exists, status is 'unverified' and conformance_verdict is null, never a guessed or inferred verdict. Reads MIDAX's own signed registry only -- makes no live request to the target, so it adds minimal latency. Always declares age_days, freshness, and verdict_source (what mechanism answered). authenticity_verdict is always present in the payload (null with an explicit note until that feature ships). next_step always carries the exact price and route for the next paid step -- never a vague 'contact us'.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The https:// URL of the x402 service you are about to pay.

200.description: Always 200 whether or not a verdict exists -- status distinguishes the two cases.

400.description: url missing or not a well-formed https:// URL.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (own bucket, separate from /verify).

get.summary: Challenge-readiness preview (free, no signature, no evidence)
get.description: The five official requirements of the Global x402 Challenge for one participant endpoint, each as pass, fail or not_measured with the time it was measured. Same engine and fail-closed rules as the paid check: a requirement that could not be measured is never shown as a pass, and a target that cannot be measured returns no partial result. No evidence, no reasons, no signature. A result is cached per target for 10 minutes and keeps its real measurement time. full_verdict gives the price and route of the signed verdict with evidence.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The https:// URL of the participant's paid x402 endpoint.

400.description: url missing, not a well-formed https:// URL, or a MIDAX URL.

422.description: The target could not be measured (no parseable 402). No partial result.

429.description: Rate limit per IP, or the hourly limit of new measurements.

503.description: An instrument failed or the measurement hit its deadline.

x402Payment.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
x402Payment.description: x402 payment proof header. Clients may also send X-PAYMENT depending on their SDK.
